analysis.one_liner: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories is an Indian pharmaceutical company making generic drugs, active pharma ingredients and biosimilars, sold mainly in the US, India, Russia/CIS and other emerging markets.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results are due on 23 October 2026, about a week away. The last two quarters have been rough: Q1 FY27 (June 2026) profit fell roughly 69% year-on-year as the windfall from generic Revlimid (lenalidomide) continues to fade, and management also flagged an unspecified 'impact related to semaglutide API' on the earnings call. Separately, three manufacturing sites (Bachupally biologics, FTO-9 Vizag, FTO-11 Pydibhimavaram) received USFDA Form 483 observations between June and October 2026 - these are preliminary inspection findings, not warning letters or import alerts, but worth watching for escalation.
analysis.plain_terms: For a couple of years, Dr. Reddy's made outsized profits selling the generic version of Revlimid, a blockbuster cancer drug, under a limited-exclusivity deal in the US. That windfall is now stepping down, so year-on-year profit comparisons look alarming (down 86% in one quarter, 69% in the next) even though this is partly a return to a more normal baseline rather than the core business collapsing. The open question is where profit settles once the comparison noise clears - and a newly flagged issue with semaglutide API supply adds a fresh uncertainty on top of that.
analysis.quarters: FY26 (year to March 2026): revenue ₹33,593 crore (+3% YoY), EBITDA ₹7,659 crore (-17% YoY, margin ~23%), PAT ₹4,285 crore (-24% YoY). Q4 FY26 revenue of ₹7,546 crore (+12% YoY) included a ₹453 crore 'Shelf Stock Adjustment' tied to excess lenalidomide inventory that management explicitly flagged as hurting comparability - stripping it out, EBITDA margin was closer to 19.5% versus the reported 13%; net profit still fell 86% YoY to about ₹220 crore. Q1 FY27 (June 2026) revenue was ₹8,099.8 crore, down 5.5% YoY but up 7.3% QoQ; PAT was about ₹440 crore, down ~69% YoY though up sharply QoQ off a low base. Q1 FY27 EBITDA was not available in a verified, consistent figure - check on Screener.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is 12.6% below its all-time peak of ₹1,394.74 (21 August 2024). A 5:1 stock split followed in October 2024, but the figures supplied are split-adjusted, so this drawdown is real price weakness, not a split artifact. Over 1 year the stock is roughly flat (-0.48%), which is actually better than the Nifty (-9.19%) and peer Cipla (-14.0%) - a relative, not absolute, win. Over 3 years it has lagged both (+13.02% vs +16.55% Nifty, +17.34% Cipla), and over 5 years it has only just kept pace with the index (+29.15% vs +24.46% Nifty) while being left well behind by Cipla (+53.14%). For a pharma major with a 30-year listing history, that is a mediocre long-run outcome.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 31-32x, the stock is priced well above the broad market even though FY26 PAT fell 24% YoY and the two most recent quarters show sharp profit declines. The 'why' it trades at this multiple appears to be optionality the market is paying for: new launches (a semaglutide injection approval in Canada), a biosimilar pipeline, and licensing deals like the Immutep oncology agreement, on the hope that profits normalize once the lenalidomide comparison cycles out. Whether that's genuinely cheap or expensive depends on confirmation that the earnings base has actually stabilized - which Q2 FY27 results (23 October 2026) will start to answer.
analysis.growth_read: FY26 revenue grew only 3% YoY while EBITDA and PAT fell 17% and 24% respectively - this is margin compression on roughly flat volumes, not margin-led growth. The underlying driver is the unwind of a one-off generic exclusivity windfall rather than a clear volume or pricing trend in the base business; how the core, ex-lenalidomide business is actually growing is not verified from available sources.
analysis.health_read: The balance sheet looks comfortable: borrowings of about ₹7,734 crore against cash and investments of roughly ₹9,851 crore implies a net cash position of around ₹2,100 crore at FY26-end. ROE of 11.2% and ROCE of 13.0% are respectable but unremarkable for a pharma major, and lower than the company's recent high base. The real concern here is business risk (earnings quality and dependence on a fading exclusive opportunity), not financial risk - the company isn't over-leveraged, but its recent profit numbers have been propped up by a windfall that is now gone. Whether reported profits are converting cleanly into operating cash flow was not verified - check the cash flow statement on Screener.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter holding has been steady at about 26.6%, held through family trusts (GVP Family Trust 11.51%, VSD Family Trust 9.06%, Kallam Satish Reddy HUF 3.31%), and promoters disclosed zero pledged shares through FY26 as of June 2026 - a clean signal. Shareholding splits between FII and public holders conflict across sources for roughly the same period (one shows FII ~20.7%/public ~20.8% as of March 2026, another shows FII ~32.1%/public ~9.6% for June/September 2026) - a swing that large in one or two quarters looks like a data or classification inconsistency rather than a real shift, so this should be checked directly against NSE/BSE shareholding filings before being treated as fact. No specific named high-profile individual investor was found on the register either way.
strengths: Net cash position of roughly ₹2,100 crore at FY26-end despite the profit decline
Zero promoter pledging disclosed through FY26
1-year return (-0.48%) beat both the Nifty (-9.19%) and peer Cipla (-14.0%)
Pipeline optionality: Canada approval for a semaglutide injection, a biosimilar pipeline, and the Immutep oncology licensing deal
watchpoints: PAT fell 86% YoY in Q4 FY26 and ~69% YoY in Q1 FY27 as the lenalidomide (gRevlimid) windfall fades - where profit stabilizes post-cliff is unresolved
Form 483 observations at three plants (Bachupally, FTO-9, FTO-11) between June and October 2026 - not yet warning letters, but worth tracking for escalation
Management cited an unspecified 'semaglutide API' impact on the Q1 FY27 call without detail on its size or duration
A P/E of ~31-32x is pricing in a profit recovery that hasn't yet shown up in reported numbers, and 3-5 year shareholder returns have trailed peer Cipla by a wide margin
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 results on 23 October 2026 - whether profit stabilizes after two straight quarters of steep YoY declines tied to the fading lenalidomide windfall, or whether the semaglutide API issue signals further deterioration.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked: FY26 and quarterly revenue/EBITDA/PAT figures across multiple news sources (Business Standard, Upstox, MarketsMojo, Angel One); promoter holding and zero-pledge disclosure; USFDA Form 483 reports; Q2 FY27 results date. Not verified: exact Q1 FY27 EBITDA figure, P/B ratio, precise nature/magnitude of the semaglutide API impact, India/Russia segment detail, and FY27 management guidance. Flagged and set aside: conflicting FII/public shareholding splits between sources for what should be the same reporting periods - verify on NSE/BSE filings before use.
